scope: Proposition 8.10 (Finite families of centered fields) of the manuscript “Scale and conformal symmetry in four-dimensional operational quantum field theory” (preprints/Scale-and-conformal-symmetry-in-four-dimensional-operational-quantum-field-theory-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 282 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 485a44682f95ef0d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 106. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let A range over a fixed finite collection of homogeneous original fields, L, and their covariant derivatives. For every fixed finite collection of depths, the corresponding centered fields B (r) A have all mutual and original-field joint products on D, with the required adjoints, locality, covariance, ordered spectra, and compatible original-net affiliated realizations. If A has real dimension ∆ and NA components, depth r has dimension ∆ − r and at most 4rNA components before field identities. These finite families satisfy the intrinsic membership criterion of Assumption 2.1. Every finite Ward word on the original fields and L is a finite sum of polynomial-coordinate multiples of derivatives of such centered fields.
